about: Unit abbreviations and fraction glyphs (loop B150, BI-133, CROSS X-057). An abbreviation's period is dropped when the sentence goes on in lowercase or a comma follows, kept at the end and before a capital; after a/an/the/this/that/each/every a fraction takes no article of its own ('a ½ mile' a half mile, 'the ¼ mile mark' the quarter mile mark, 'the 3/4 mile mark' the three quarter mile mark); fractions glued to mph/kg/lb/oz read with the unit ('¾ kg' three quarters of a kilogram, '2½ mph' two and a half miles an hour); kg/lb/lbs/oz/t after a number are kilograms/pounds/ounces/tons, a weight between a determiner and a noun is singular ('a 5 lb bag' a five pound bag). Guards: Mt./St., 'a lb of', t-shirts, final periods. X-057 wording '½ mi.' is 'a half mile' here (Backseat's distance goldens say 'a half mile', not 'half a mile'). Backseat Driver: backseat::pronunciation::ForSpeech (libs/backseat/backseat_tests/pronunciation_test.cpp).
